KIRAN MISHRA ETC. Petiti  VERSUS  THE STATE OF JHARKHAND & ANR. Respon  IA No. 227961/2024 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 Date : 09-04-2025
This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SUDHANSHU DHULIA
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN

For Petitioner(s) Mr. K. Parameshwar, Sr.Adv.
 Mr. Ayush Anand, AOR  Mr. Srinivas Patil, Adv.
 Mr. Rohan Mazumdar, Adv.
 Ms. Neeharika Mazumdar, Adv.
 For Respondent(s) Mr. Kumar Anurag Singh, Adv.
 Ms. Madhusmita Bora, AOR  Mr. Dipankar Singh, Adv.
 Mr. Neeraj Kumar Verma, AOR  Mr. M.A. Niyazi, Adv.
 Ms. Anamika Ghai Niyazi, Adv.
 Ms. Kirti Kumari, Adv.
 Ms. Nehmat Sethi, Adv.
 Mr. Arquam Ali, Adv.
Kiran Mishra vs The State Of Jharkhand on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65627738/
1  UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R
The petitioners were accused in FIR No. 256/13, dated 03.08.2013, registered under Sections 323/406/498A/504/506 IPC at P.S. Bistapur by the second respondent.
Petitioner No.1 is the sister-in-law and petitioner No.2 is the husband of the complainant.
There has been some procedural lapse on the part of the petitioners, which cannot be denied as much as they have not surrendered before the High Court, as is the requirement under the law.
Therefore, their applications for exemption from surrendering were dismissed by the High Court.

Vide order dated 16.12.2024, the second petitioner was directed to pay the entire dues to respondent No.2 before the next date of hearing, failing which the interim protection granted to the petitioners shall stand vacated.
Today, during the course of hearing, it is submitted that the entire dues have already been transferred to the account of the complainant.

Taking into consideration the fact that if petitioner No.2 is taken into custody, he will lose his job as also the fact that petitioner No.1 is the sister-in-law of respondent No.2 and petitioner No.2 is the husband of respondent No.2, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioners exemption from surrendering should be allowed.
Accordingly, the petitioners are presently exempted from surrendering.
Let the petitioners appear before the court concerned within a period of one week and move an appropriate application.
The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the above terms.
As a result, the pending interlocutory application also stands disposed of.

(SATISH KUMAR YADAV) (RENU BALA GAMBHIR)
